title: Nose and sinus rinse
what: An ENT doctor rinses your nose and sinuses with a salt or medicated solution to clear out mucus and pus. No needles and no cuts.
why: For a runny nose, sinusitis, or enlarged adenoids, when your nose is blocked and the mucus does not come out on its own.
duration: one session usually takes 10 to 15 minutes; a course is usually 5 to 10 sessions
tell_doctor: Allergy to medicines or nose drops
If you have a high fever or an earache now

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat, but avoid a big meal for 1 hour before. You may gag.

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: Blow your nose before the procedure. The doctor will put in drops that reduce swelling.

prepare.title: For children
prepare.text: Tell your child ahead of time that it will feel a bit wet and tickly, but it will not hurt.

bring: Sinus X-rays or CT scan, if you had them
steps: You sit or lie down, with your head tilted back a little
The doctor puts drops in your nose to reduce swelling and waits a few minutes
Warm solution is slowly poured into one nostril
A machine suctions it out of the other nostril together with mucus
To keep the solution out of your throat, you are asked to keep saying 'coo-coo'
Then the same is done on the other side
feel: A feeling of water in your nose and pressure at the bridge of your nose
Your eyes may water and you may want to sneeze. This is normal
It should not hurt. If it feels bad, signal the doctor
after: Some solution may drip from your nose for 10 to 20 minutes
For about 1 hour, stay out of frost and cold wind
Breathing usually gets easier after the first few sessions
red_flags: Swelling and redness around the eye, a bad headache, or a high fever: see a doctor right away
A nosebleed that does not stop in 20 minutes: call emergency services

faq.q: Why do I say 'coo-coo' during the rinse?
faq.a: It makes the soft palate close the way to your throat, so the solution does not drain there. That is why some people call it the 'cuckoo' rinse.

faq.q: Is the rinse a sinus puncture?
faq.a: No. The solution is poured in and suctioned out through the nostrils, with no needles or punctures.
